title: Low Exposed Bedrock Shelf — Ukrainian Steppe Granite Outcrop
era: Natural feature (Proterozoic exposed granite, Ukrainian crystalline shield / Азово-Подільський щит)

sources.shield_geology: Ukrainian crystalline shield (Азово-Подільський щит / Azov-Podolian Shield) — Encyclopedia of Ukraine, vol. V (Toronto, 1993); Ukrainian Shield = Precambrian granite-gneiss basement exposed by Cenozoic erosion in the steppe zone, dominantly coarse-grained grey biotite-granite and gneiss
sources.outcrop_class: Twidale C.R. & Vidal Romani J.R. 'Landforms and Geology of Granite Terrains' (Taylor & Francis, 2005), Chapter 4 — classification of low bedrock exposures: 'low outcrop' (pavements and low shields) = 0.10–0.50 m above surrounding soil, plan span 0.3–3.0 m; abundant on flat interfluves of dissected shields
sources.ecotone_hard_rock: Sharp steppe-to-forest-steppe ecotone edge on hard rock substrates (vs. diffuse edge on loess) — Erdős et al. 2018, Applied Vegetation Science 21:475–488; Chytrý et al. 2022, Journal of Vegetation Science 33:e13136
sources.granite_colour: Ukrainian Shield granite colour: medium grey (Munsell N5–N6) on fresh faces, warm iron-ochre staining (10YR 5/4–6/6) on long-exposed upper surfaces — Lazarenko E.K. 'Mineralogy of Ukraine' (1975), Kyiv; field observations in the Ukrainian Geological Survey (ГСУ) crystalline basement mapping reports
sources.moss_lichen: Crustose and foliose lichens (Parmelia sulcata, Rhizocarpon geographicum) and thin bryophyte cushions (Grimmia pulvinata) colonise steppe granite outcrops; green-grey lichen crust 5–25 mm thick on sheltered depressions and shaded upper faces — Kondratyuk S.Ya. et al. (2007) 'Checklist of Lichens of Ukraine', NASU, Kyiv; also Makarova I.I. 'Mosses of Rock Outcrops' in Bot. Zhurn. 82(1), 1997
sources.steppe_grass_margin: Dry grass (Festuca valesiaca, Stipa capillata) and stonecrop (Sedum acre) occupy thin skeletal soil pockets at rock margins and crevices in the Ukrainian steppe — Encyclopedia of Ukraine, 'Steppe' article; Didukh Ya.P. (2009) 'Red Data Book of Ukrainian vegetation' on rocky steppe communities

rock_type.mineralogy: Coarse-grained grey biotite-granite; k-feldspar phenocrysts 10–30 mm; colour N5–N6 grey unweathered, iron-ochre stained on exposed summit faces

height_range_mm.note: Low outcrop class (Twidale 2005); design = 400 mm incl. 20 mm lichen/moss crown

plan_range_mm.note: Small shelf exposure; main rock block 1200 mm length × 800 mm width

layer_derivation.derivation_note: Rock stack (floor to apex): base slab 80 mm + main body 140 mm + upper shelf 100 mm + crest 60 mm = 380 mm granite. Width tapers each layer by ~15–20% to approximate weathered, rounded form. Offsets (±30–60 mm in x and z) mimic irregular joint-controlled erosion. All values within the 100–500 mm low-outcrop height range.

moss_dimensions.note: Lichen/bryophyte crust modeled as 20 mm thick bevelBox on exposed upper faces — within the 5–25 mm range from literature

grass_tuft.note: Festuca/Stipa tuft 100 mm tall × 100 mm wide × 80 mm deep; placed just outside rock base perimeter in thin skeletal soil

Dry grass tufts at rock margin
